alice: quick heads-up — running nightly perf on llama3-13b surfaced a regression after the kernel routing tweak. p99 token latency jumps ~28% for chat_template workloads at long seqs (>=1024). attaching quick trace link: https://perftool.local/trace/3490012345
ben: thanks. is this only with the new rope_theta default or across all variants?
carmen: i saw something similar in canary earlier but assumed it's kv-evict churn. can you paste the trace highlights?
alice: main smell: kernel selector flips from fused-attn->fallback path at step ~1200 tokens. stack shows mismatched head dim path chosen when seq len + cached KV > threshold. excerpt: ```SelectedKernel: fallback_matmul_v2 -> latency +22ms per token at 2048 seq```
dmitri: repro command I used: ```./perf_runner --model=llama3-13b --config=configs/chat_template.json --batch=4 --max_tokens=2048 --warmup=200``` see perf-bot trace (same id)
perf-bot: nightly-run 3490012345: p50=9.2ms p95=18.8ms p99=42.4ms (baseline p99=33.1ms). mem snapshots show KV cache spikes during kernel switch.
eva: hypothesis: rope_theta routing change altered the head-dim alignment predicate in kernel-selector. for some head sizes the fused rmsnorm+attn kernel expects stride-aligned KV layout; when predicate fails we fallback to generic matmul.
ben: can we short-circuit selector to force fused path for repro?
dmitri: yes, temp override: ```env KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCED=fused_rms_attn ./perf_runner ...``` did that — p99 returned to 34ms. so selector logic is root cause.
carmen: related note: chat_template pads prefixes => mixed short+long seqs in same batch cause dynamic kernel choices mid-batch. batching heuristic should isolate similar seq-length groups. we should avoid mixing prefix-heavy chat with end-user short messages.
alice: agree. two action items I propose: 1) add a quick-fix in selector to prefer fused_rms_attn when head_dim % 32 == 0 and kv_layout == packed. 2) update batching heuristic to bucket by (prefix_length_bucket, total_seq_bucket).
eva: also want to audit rope_theta default change — the new slope moved effective rotation frequency which changes precomputed sin/cos tiled layout used by some kernels. small theta drift can change whether we use optimized rotary-embedding fused kernels.
ben: test plan: add unit test for selector with variations: head_dim: [64,80,96], rope_theta: [0.997,1.0,1.23], seq: [128,1024,2048], kv_cached: [true,false]. ensure chosen kernel stays stable across iterations.
dmitri: i'll throw together a smoke patch in runtime selector and run a 2h canary on dedicated-qa pool. patch will log selector predicate inputs (head_dim, rope_theta, kv_layout, batch_seq_dist) to help tune heuristics.
carmen: small thing — RMSNorm impl toggles between fused/non-fused can alter memory layout (NHWC vs NCHW style buffs) which breaks some low-level kernel fast paths. align those too.
perf-bot: created ticket RI-6458: "kernel-selector: guard fused attn path with head/kv/rope invariants" assigned to eng-runtime.
alice: thanks. dmitri, file a short perf note in the runtime wiki after you validate canary. i'll hold off on rolling the rope_theta default until we patch selector. :thumbsup:
